messages.content: How much gas is generated from heating a 2 m³ closed chamber with air at a temperature of 25°C to 100°C?

function.name: thermodynamics_calc_gas_pressure
function.description: Calculate gas pressure in a closed chamber due to heating Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

volume.description: The volume of the chamber in cubic meters. This is a float type value.

initial_temperature.description: The initial temperature of the gas in degree Celsius. This is a float type value.

final_temperature.description: The final temperature of the gas in degree Celsius. This is a float type value.

initial_pressure.description: The initial pressure of the gas in Pascal. Default is standard atmospheric pressure. This is a float type value.

message.reasoning: The user asks: "How much gas is generated from heating a 2 m³ closed chamber with air at a temperature of 25°C to 100°C?" They want to know how much gas is generated? But it's a closed chamber, so no gas generation? Maybe they mean expansion? Actually, heating air in a closed chamber will increase pressure but not generate more gas. So answer: no additional gas is generated; the amount remains constant. The volume is fixed, so the amount of gas (moles) stays same. The pressure increases. We can calculate new pressure using ideal gas law: P1V = nRT1, P2V = nRT2 => P2 = P1 * T2/T1. If initial pressure is standard atmospheric ~101325 Pa. Temperature in Kelvin: T1=298K, T2=373K. So P2 = 101325 * 373/298 ≈ 126,800 Pa. So pressure increases by about 25%. But no gas generation. So answer accordingly.
